- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, true price often rebounds — adjust downward forecast by 3–8% after peak.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16) and price is rising, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 1–3% to forecast for 10–15 day horizon.
- If model forecast is > 5% above recent 18-day average, and sentiment is negative, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid over-optimism.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.16) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply 1–3% downward correction after 5–7 day trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is > 10% above model, and sentiment is positive, model likely missed momentum — adjust upward by 1–4% for next 10 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and model forecast is rising, model may be ignoring bearish sentiment — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
